column1: # Canonical machine tokens, their match sites, and the tolerance of each reader.
# mika#2201. ONE source of truth, two readers: scripts/check-canonical-tokens.sh
# (the lint) and canonical_tokens::tests::mika2201_every_match_site_is_declared
# (the exhaustiveness scan).
# THE RULE THIS FILE ENCODES, AND WHY IT IS NOT "MACHINE TOKENS ARE ENGLISH"
# Prime's bearing: ticket prose is French, machine tokens are exact canonical
# English. Confronted to the code that matches — which is Prime's own closing
# bound — the naive reading of that rule accuses two shapes this repository
# reads DELIBERATELY WELL: `seconde passe` (bilingual by written decision in
# `grooming_marker.rs` since mika#2158) and the paraphrase tier of
# `_parse_disposition`. A lint red on the day it is born gets disarmed, and then
# the regression it exists to catch passes in the noise.
# So the discriminator is the TOLERANCE OF THE READER, never the language of
# the token:
#   class A — the reader READS the variant. The lint stays silent, entirely.
#   class B — the reader MIS-reads it. The lint fires, per the axes below.
# `tolérance` is a WIRE FORMAT, consumed by the lint one rule at a time:
#   exact:line-anchored   `(?m)^…` / `grep -E '^…'` — position and case fixed
#   exact:word-boundary   `\b…\b` — case fixed, position free
#   exact:prefix          `starts_with` / `strip_prefix` — byte-exact prefix
#   exact:suffix          `ends_with` — byte-exact, anchored at the TAIL. Not
#                         `exact:literal`: the position is part of the read, and
#                         that is the whole discriminator between a marker and a
#                         prose that merely mentions it (mika#2050's class).
#   exact:literal         `grep -F`, `match_indices`, substring equality
#   ci:line-anchored      `(?i)` — CASE IS READ; rule L2 must NOT fire here
#   ci+emphasis:…         `(?i)` plus a markdown-emphasis run (mika#1828)
#   paraphrase            a fuzzy tier reads reworded forms
#   ci+fr:…               case-insensitive plus the listed French forms
# A token whose tolerance carries `ci` is one the lint may not accuse of case.
# That column is the whole reason this file exists rather than a list of
# spellings: without it, an author starting from the naive rule accuses every
# class A row on his first run.
# HOW EACH HALF IS MAINTAINED, AND WHERE THE GUARANTEE STOPS
# TWO GUARDS, TWO DIRECTIONS, AND NEITHER IS THE OTHER'S COPY.
#   `canonical-tokens-survey.sh --check` starts from the reading FORM. Every
#   strict site it finds must appear here, in either class. An undeclared one
#   fails the build. Resolution is always to DECLARE — never to allowlist. A
#   match site nobody wants to declare is a match site to delete (§ D5/D6).
#   `canonical_tokens::tests::mika2201_every_match_site_is_declared` starts from
#   the TOKEN, which lets it see a reader the survey cannot — `contains` is not
#   a survey form, measured: admitting it adds fourteen false rows for two real
#   ones. `check_grooming_markers` below was found that way.
#   `…::mika2201_every_declared_symbol_still_exists` holds the STALE direction,
#   by checking that each `chemin::symbole` still names something. That is the
#   question asked directly, rather than inferred from a coincidence with a
#   survey that structurally cannot produce a `(?i)` alternation or a fuzzy
#   tier. Residual rot it does not catch, named rather than hidden: a row whose
#   file and symbol both still exist but which no longer reads the token.
# Named consequence of classing by tolerance rather than by form: a strict site
# could be written class A to escape the lint. That is a hand edit to a reviewed
# file, not a silent drift, and its symbol is still checked.
# A `.github/labels.yml` site is out of the survey's perimeter by construction
# (it is not source) and is never compared in either direction.
# jeton
# ═══ Class A — TOLERANT readers. Out of the lint's perimeter, BY MEASUREMENT.
# These rows are the reason this file exists. Without them, an author starting
# from "machine token = exact English" accuses every one of them — which is the
# failure mode mika#2201 § R4 names, reached by its own remedy.
# Not produced by the survey: `(?i)` alternations and fuzzy tiers are not strict
# reading forms.
second-pass
